before.notes: Therapeutic radiotherapy trial using lattice RT or SBRT for large inoperable tumors, or tumors for which radiotherapy is preferred to surgery. Tumor-specific screening is required.

after.title: Lattice or SBRT radiotherapy for large inoperable canine tumors
after.center: University of Zurich — Division of Radiation Oncology
after.status: Ongoing European oncology clinical trial — listed by Oncowaf
after.funding: 🟠 Partially funded. Owners pay the initial consultation, radiation-planning CT and anesthesia for the radiation treatments. Research funding covers the radiation itself and CT or MRI follow-up examinations at six and twelve months.
after.notes: Randomized therapeutic comparison of Lattice radiotherapy and SBRT for large inoperable canine tumors, or when radiotherapy is preferred to surgery. Five consecutive daily treatment sessions. Research biopsies are requested when safely accessible; the treating team confirms final eligibility and consent. Single enrolling center: University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital.

before.title: Fluorescence-guided surgery for canine peripheral nerve sheath / plexus tumors
before.center: Universitäres Tierspital Zürich / University of Zurich
before.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with the University of Zurich study team.
before.notes: Therapeutic surgical study for peripheral nerve sheath/plexus tumors using fluorescence guidance to improve tumor visualization and potentially enable limb-preserving surgery. PNST-specific; other STS are not automatically eligible.

after.title: Fluorescence-guided surgery for canine peripheral nerve sheath / plexus tumors
after.center: Universitäres Tierspital Zürich / University of Zurich
after.funding: 🟠 Partially funded. Research funding provides the study fluorescence dye free of charge. The primary protocol does not itemize coverage of staging, surgery or other care; confirm these costs with the Zurich study team.
after.notes: Therapeutic surgical study comparing ICG and Angiostamp fluorescence guidance for canine brachial or lumbar plexus tumors; target enrollment40 dogs, ethics ZH026/2023. Suspected plexus tumor on CT/MRI and planned resection are sufficient for prescreening: cytology is helpful but explicitly not mandatory because sampling may be infeasible. PNST-specific; other soft-tissue sarcomas are not automatically eligible. Single enrolling center: University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital.

before.title: Fluorescence-guided surgery for soft tissue sarcoma
before.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with University of Zurich.
before.notes: Current European oncology listing for fluorescence-guided sarcoma surgery in dogs and cats. Investigator prescreening is required.

after.title: Fluorescence-guided surgery for soft tissue sarcoma
after.funding: 🟠 Partially funded. Swiss National Science Foundation research funding covers the main part of the surgery cost. The exact percentage and coverage of staging, anesthesia, hospitalization and other care are not itemized publicly; confirm the owner-paid balance with the Zurich study team.
after.notes: Therapeutic surgical study comparing ICG and Angiostamp fluorescence guidance for dogs and cats with confirmed soft-tissue sarcoma requiring excision or re-excision after incomplete surgery. Surgery is adjusted to remove fluorescent residual tumor tissue. Severe cardiac/renal disease that prevents anesthesia excludes participation; final eligibility is investigator-confirmed. Single enrolling center: University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital. This general soft-tissue sarcoma cohort is distinct from the canine plexus/PNST cohort despite shared ethics identifier ZH026/2023.

before.status: Participation currently possible on the University of Zurich study page
before.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with University of Zurich.
before.notes: Current University of Zurich study evaluating ultra-high-dose-rate FLASH proton radiotherapy for cats with oral squamous cell carcinoma.

after.title: FLASH proton radiotherapy for feline oral squamous cell carcinoma
after.status: Participation currently possible on the University of Zurich study page
after.contacts: University of Zurich study team — Dr. Maximilian Körner; +41 44 635 95 55; onkologie@vetclinics.uzh.ch
after.funding: 🟠 Partially funded. Owners pay half the initial diagnostic work-up cost: imaging, biopsy and blood tests. The official study flyer states that no further costs arise from the time of study enrollment. Confirm the current estimate and any unrelated care with the Zurich study team.
after.notes: Current randomized study comparing FLASH and conventional proton radiotherapy for cats with oral squamous cell carcinoma, including tongue tumors. Radiation is given on three consecutive days at the Paul Scherrer Institute; cats remain hospitalized for four days at the University of Zurich Veterinary Hospital. Zurich handles enrollment and inpatient veterinary care; PSI is the radiation-delivery partner, not a separate owner-enrollment clinic. Initial CT and biopsy establish tumor extent/type; a temporary feeding tube is placed for treatment. Clinical follow-ups are weekly in month1 and every three months in year1, with CT at6,12,18 months. Final eligibility is confirmed by the study team.
